views.markdown: An iOS developer framework for unified hooking methods.

Publish-before-activation across every backend, an explicit inline-guard state machine, and a fully on-device-validated backend matrix (all nine backends, zero crashes).

**The architecture change:** originals are now published into the caller's cell *before* a replacement becomes reachable, on every path — fishhook publishes through the rebind-scan callback before the first GOT slot write, native seals the trampoline before `hk_write`, Frida publishes while staged before `end_transaction`, litehook rebind publishes before the scan, and the rebuilt Dobby lib writes `*out_origin_func` before the trampoline commit. Providers that cannot guarantee the ordering (ElleKit's hooking, litehook-inline) refuse requested originals with side-effect-free `HK_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED` instead of exposing a NULL-original window (the PC=0 crash class).

**Also in this tag (since 2.2.5-1):**
- Inline guard: explicit PENDING/INSTALLED/TAINTED states with generation tokens — pending duplicates refuse instead of waiting, tainted entries are hard errors, stale settles are dropped (no false-idempotent success)
- Queue-always batching restores v1 semantics: every supported hook queues while batching is on, nothing applies until `executeHooks`
- ElleKit/libhooker ABI detection by observable export (`EKHookFunction`), fail-closed on unknown providers; publication policy resolves at runtime per detected ABI
- fishhook: page-protection restore (no more permanently-writable GOT pages), matched/failed result accounting, reentrancy-pinned rebind entries, partial failures reported honestly (`HK_ERR_PARTIAL`)
- litehook: unsafe shared-cache parser removed (private-symbol lookups fall back to the native bounded parser)
- Dobby: vendored static lib rebuilt from upstream 5dfc854 with the publication-reorder patch (instruction-verified in both slices), inline policy flipped to BeforeActivation
- Shared ARM64 preflight split: backend-independent basic checks always run (alignment, self-hook, executable mappings); the fixed-window terminator/literal scan gates only the weak fixed-window relocators (Dobby, litehook) — ElleKit/Substrate/Substitute/Frida let their own relocators decide
- NULL original cell when none requested — vendors use their documented smaller-hook mode
- Descriptor-driven backend capabilities (hook-kind masks incl. memory), owner-tagged image handles with a registry (cross-backend use rejected, double-close safe), boundary validation on all public inputs
- Swift: method-kind/instance validation, PAC strip-then-sign, nlist symbols signed only for instruction sections
- Provenance: `vendor/VENDORED.md` with byte-verified upstream pins, vendored Apache-2.0/wxWindows/BSD-4 license files; roothide packages now gate `firmware (>= 15.0)`

**On-device verification** (iPhone 7, iOS 15.8.3, ElleKit, ShadowHarness): full backend matrix — fishhook rebind (live + zero-match fail-closed), ElleKit inline (incl. policy refusals), rebuilt Dobby, native engine, Frida inline + batch transaction, litehook rebind, Substrate, memory patch — all green; zero crashes across all rounds; Shadow 3.7.6 and 4.0.0 compatibility confirmed.

Packages: iphoneos-arm (rooted), iphoneos-arm64 (rootless), iphoneos-arm64e (roothide).

Fix the batch deferred-original crash that broke v1-era consumers (e.g. Shadow 3.7.6) against HookKit v2.

**The bug:** HookKit v2's batched installs wrote originals into the caller's %orig cells only after the *entire* batch drain returned. A replacement installed earlier in the same batch was live while its %orig cell was still NULL — so any mid-batch re-entry into it (ElleKit's patch writer calls vm_region_recurse_64, which Shadow's Hook_Memory group hooks) called NULL and crashed (SIGSEGV at PC 0, reproduced on-device in 4/4 apps at launch). v1 never hit this: caller cells were the libhooker out-pointers, so each original published the moment its hook applied.

**The fix:** publish originals at apply time (v1 semantics) — batched function hooks use the caller's cell as the out-pointer (batch-owned cell as fallback), message-hook originals are written immediately, and origValue is synced afterward so the drain's non-NULL invariant and inline-guard settlement still see the real original. On-device verified: Shadow 3.7.6 launches the previously crashing apps cleanly.

Also in this tag (2.2.4-1 + 2.2.5-1 since 2.2.3-1):
- ElleKit ABI detection reverted to the tested filename discriminator (LHStrError is exported by both ElleKit and real libhooker, so symbol cross-checks fail closed against legitimate ElleKit installs)
- litehook: global-rebind list index fix (underflow on first insert, overwrite on later inserts)
- Availability introspection restores the compile-time backends (fishhook/litehook/native/dobby/swift) to getAvailableSubstitutorTypes/getAvailableCategories

Packages: iphoneos-arm (rooted), iphoneos-arm64 (rootless), iphoneos-arm64e (roothide).
